clue.text: Maiden possibly facing accusation as cheat

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, so a maiden is one kind of over
a charge is a formal accusation

explanation.surface: A young woman faces an accusation of cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman, but here it is the cricket term: a maiden over is six balls without a run conceded.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcharge someone is to swindle them by asking too much money, a form of cheating.

clue.text: Look after seaman in capital city

indicators.note: after places the word for look behind the seaman's letters

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look after a sailor in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'take care of', but 'after' is a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: English witness wants capture of top person who's got away

indicators.note: the witness word wants to capture, i.e. enclose, the top word

parts.note: to witness something is to see it
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: An English witness wants an escaped top villain caught.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has escaped, a fugitive who got away.

clue.text: Join branch of police and achieve legal recognition

parts.note: to come into a business or family is to join it
a police force is a regional branch of the police, e.g. the Met

explanation.surface: A recruit joins a police branch and wins official recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or rule that comes into force becomes legally effective, gaining legal standing.

clue.text: A quiet break interrupted by onset of loud cheers?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: the break word is split open by the letter that follows

parts.note: a pause is a short break

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hushed pause is broken by the start of loud cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by onset of loud' puts L inside PAUSE to give PLAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is clapping and cheering; the question mark admits cheers are only one kind.

clue.text: Shrub getting good 'ack?

parts.note: a hack is a horse; dropping the H, as a Cockney might, gives 'ack for hack, so 'orse for horse

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a shrub is a good 'ack, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe tells the solver to drop the H throughout: 'ack is hack, a riding horse, which becomes 'orse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub, also called furze or whin.

clue.text: Drink nothing, coming back for work

indicators.note: coming back tells us to read the drink and nothing words from right to left

parts.note: to sup is to drink
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone drinks nothing on returning to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: IRA member on street becomes a dignitary

parts.note: a Provo is a member of the Provisional IRA

explanation.surface: A former IRA man becomes a civic dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A provost is a senior official, such as the head of a Scottish council or of certain colleges.

clue.text: Something in tool shed maybe has left little darlings upset — snake

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the darlings word is read bottom to top

parts.note: pets are favourites or darlings
an adder is a snake

explanation.surface: Something in the shed has frightened the children: a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a folding ladder often kept in a tool shed, among other places.

clue.text: Officer returning with hesitation as one to fill a gap?

indicators.note: returning means the officer abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A returning officer hesitates over who will fill a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer returning' suggests a returning officer at an election; 'returning' actually reverses COL to LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who stands in temporarily, filling a vacancy.

clue.text: Optical instrument must be awfully precise when surgery's involved

indicators.note: involved means the surgery word is wrapped inside the rearranged letters
awfully suggests the word precise is badly mangled and rearranged

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: An optical instrument must be extremely precise when used in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' reads as an intensifier ('awfully precise') but signals the anagram, giving PERISCE; 'involved' is the containment signal, not a description of surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A periscope uses mirrors or prisms to let a viewer see over obstacles, an optical device.

clue.text: Conservative in party flexible — one out to impress superiors

indicators.note: in means the Conservative letter sits inside the joined party and flexible words

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering
limber means supple or flexible

explanation.surface: A flexible Tory at a party is out to impress his betters.
explanation.definitionFit: A social climber seeks acceptance in a higher class, trying to win favour with those above.

clue.text: Soldiers calm when guarding hospital or academic institution

parts.note: privates are soldiers of the lowest rank

indicators.note: guarding means the calm word surrounds the hospital letter

parts.note: cool means calm

explanation.surface: Calm soldiers guard a hospital or a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A private school is a fee-paying educational establishment, independent of the state.

clue.text: Not following official line, could make some gaffes

indicators.note: could make tells us the letters of some gaffes can be remade into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A politician straying from the party line could make a few blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off-message means departing from the agreed party position, as a politician might.

clue.text: Quickest run by runner in Hants

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a runner is a river; the Test is a river in Hampshire (Hants)

explanation.surface: The fastest run comes from a runner somewhere in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the short name for Hampshire, an English county; the River Test flows through it. 'Runner' sounds like an athlete but means a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift, so the superlative form means the swiftest of all.

clue.text: Dissolute editor stopped indulging completely

parts.note: fast, in the old sense, means dissolute or loose-living

explanation.surface: A debauched editor gives up his indulgences entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food altogether, a complete abstention.

clue.text: Male in the manner of rugby player who couldn't find the right words?

definitions.text: who couldn't find the right words?

parts.note: a la (French) means in the style of
a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A man like a rugby player struggles to find the right words.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Malaprop, in Sheridan's play The Rivals, comically misuses words.
explanation.definitionFit: The character Mrs Malaprop habitually substituted wrong, similar-sounding words, giving us 'malapropism'.

clue.text: Government department has uncertainty with unknown change

parts.note: MoD is the Ministry of Defence, a UK government department
an if is a doubt or uncertainty
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A government department is unsure, facing change and the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something is to alter it, a direct synonym for change.

clue.text: Figure in endless pain after a month

indicators.note: after places the pain piece behind the month

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, a month

indicators.note: endless means the pain word loses its final letter

parts.note: agony is great pain

explanation.surface: Someone is in endless pain after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a ten-sided geometric figure, a plane shape.

clue.text: Steward in club at Etihad Stadium with one short request

parts.note: Manchester City, abbreviated Man C, play at the Etihad Stadium
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: short means the request word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request

explanation.surface: A steward at Manchester City's ground makes a brief request.
explanation.definitionFit: A manciple was an officer buying provisions for a college or inn, a kind of steward.

clue.text: Servant eating too much stew

indicators.note: eating means the servant word takes in the too much word

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
OTT stands for over the top, i.e. too much

explanation.surface: A servant is eating far too much stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottage is a thick soup or stew, as in Esau's mess of pottage.

clue.text: One with exaggerated respect for priests could become so strait-laced

definitions.text: One with exaggerated respect for priests

indicators.note: could become says the letters of so strait-laced can turn into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Excessive reverence for priests might make someone so prim.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacerdotalism is belief in the priesthood's special power; an adherent gives clergy exaggerated deference.

clue.text: Bird in roofless building overlooking lake

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue puts the first piece above the lake letter
roofless in a down clue means the building word loses its top letter

parts.note: a house is a building

explanation.surface: A bird nests in a ruined building overlooking a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roofless' removes H from HOUSE, leaving OUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird, and also the ring ouzel.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement bringing change

indicators.note: revolutionary indicates the movement word turned around, read upward in this down clue

parts.note: a tide is a movement or trend, as in a tide of opinion

explanation.surface: A revolutionary movement brings about change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary movement' reads as a political uprising; 'Revolutionary' just turns TIDE round.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise or alter it.

clue.text: Gross rage may come from this belligerent person

indicators.note: may come from this says the words gross rage are produced by rearranging the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Extreme anger may be expected from a warlike individual.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs backwards: rearranging the answer gives 'gross rage', which has the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is one who attacks first or is hostile, a belligerent party.

clue.text: Bosses of firm lacking enthusiasm, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is said out loud and spelt another way

parts.note: bored means uninterested, lacking enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A firm's bosses are reportedly unenthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's directors, collectively, run the firm, forming its governing body.

clue.text: Long periods of leisure on sabbatical

indicators.note: of signals letters taken from the following words, which contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone on sabbatical enjoys long stretches of free time.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across leisurE ON Sabbatical.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are immensely long ages of time.

clue.text: Tense learner at university, outwardly faultless

indicators.note: outwardly means the faultless word sits on the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: perfect means faultless
L, from learner-driver plates, means learner
to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A nervous student at university appears flawless on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the student but is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The pluperfect, or past perfect, is a verb tense, as in 'had gone'.
